</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span><span id="S4.T3.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Each stage controls a distinct dimension: <math id="S4.T3.m72" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Loc and <math id="S4.T3.m73" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Gen cost <math id="S4.T3.m74" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.T3.m75" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14</annotation></semantics></math>pp ASR, <math id="S4.T3.m76" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Gen the most realism (<math id="S4.T3.m77" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.15</annotation></semantics></math>), <math id="S4.T3.m78" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Cur the most action balance (<math id="S4.T3.m79" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.070" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.070</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.070</annotation></semantics></math>).</span> Ablation on the 100-sample subset; top block disables one stage, lower block is <math id="S4.T3.m80" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> vs. Full. <em id="S4.T3.10" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Realism</em>: LLM-judge mean; <em id="S4.T3.11" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Goal/Action <math id="S4.T3.m81" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math></em>: normalised entropies; <em id="S4.T3.12" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">CLIP <math id="S4.T3.m82" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math></em>: mean pairwise distance. <span id="S4.T3.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bold</span>/<span id="S4.T3.14" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">underline</span> = best/second.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>RQ3: Pipeline contribution</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each pipeline stage targets a distinct subset of attack properties, so no two-stage simplification reproduces the full attack distribution. We test this by disabling one stage at a time—<math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Loc</span>, <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Gen</span>, and <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Cur</span>, defined in the stage analyses below—on the ablation subset of §<a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> (full specifications in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS3" title="B.3 Ablation Variants ‣ Appendix B Implementation Details ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>). The decomposition is validated if each variant degrades a different combination of the four measured dimensions—ASR, realism, screenshot diversity, and four-category action entropy (Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.3 RQ2: Stealth ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The Localizer governs reach (ASR and coverage).</span> Replacing it with a largest-text-region heuristic costs <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12</annotation></semantics></math>pp of ASR on both agents and lowers screenshot CLIP distance and four-category action entropy, while realism is unchanged (Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.3 RQ2: Stealth ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). The Localizer thus controls <em id="S4.SS4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">where</em> attacks land, not how they look: the heuristic often selects a non-injectable region and almost never a text-input field, so <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Loc cannot produce <span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">inject_text</span> samples (<math id="S4.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10/11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10/11</annotation></semantics></math> intents).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The Generator governs payload quality (ASR and realism jointly).</span> A fixed per-intent template costs ASR comparably (<math id="S4.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-12</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-14</annotation></semantics></math>pp) <em id="S4.SS4.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">and</em> produces the largest realism drop of any variant (<math id="S4.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.15</annotation></semantics></math>), falling most on the semantic-consistency and detectability criteria. It is the only stage that targets effectiveness and plausibility together: template payloads read as system banners, which agents treat as out-of-distribution even at a valid injection region.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The Curator governs distribution shape (realism and balance).</span> Disabling it yields the smallest ASR drop of the three variants (<math id="S4.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-6</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S4.SS4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-8</annotation></semantics></math>pp) but a measurable realism cost (<math id="S4.SS4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.12</annotation></semantics></math>) and the largest action-entropy drop (<math id="S4.SS4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.070" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.070</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.070</annotation></semantics></math>): without filtering, balance-trim, and coverage-repair, mass concentrates on the easily generated <span id="S4.SS4.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">click</span>-like intents rather than the near-uniform eleven-intent coverage that RQ1 relies on.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS4.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The three stage profiles are distinct.</span> No two target the same subset of properties, so no two-stage collapse reproduces the full attack distribution and each stage is individually necessary. Per-criterion breakdowns and ablation caveats are in Appendices <a href="#A2.SS7" title="B.7 Pipeline Decomposition: Ablation Results ‣ Appendix B Implementation Details ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.7</span></a> and <a href="#A2.SS5" title="B.5 Per-RQ Procedure ‣ Appendix B Implementation Details ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this paper, we present <span id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span>, the first automated pipeline for generating realistic, context-aware visual prompt-injection benchmarks against VLM-based GUI agents, without modifying the agent, application, or operating system. Across five agents, ten applications, and eleven attack intents, every evaluated agent is vulnerable and per-sample realism does not predict attack success—so visual-quality filtering alone cannot reliably separate injected content from benign screens, and effective defenses must act on payload semantics, action grounding, or the application’s notion of user-controllable surface.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Limitations</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Agent coverage.</span> We evaluate five VLM-based GUI agents accessed through inference APIs (the closed-weight <span id="S6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-mini</span>, the open-weight <span id="S6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GLM-4.5V</span>, and three sizes of the Qwen3-VL family). We exclude native GUI-specialised agents that require local GPU hosting, such as UI-TARS, UI-Venus, and MAI-UI, so whether purpose-built GUI agents are as vulnerable as general VLM backbones behind an action wrapper remains untested; RQ3 uses Qwen3-VL-32B only as a stand-in for such a model. Confirming the same vulnerability on locally hosted specialists is left to future work.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Single-screenshot, single-step evaluation.</span> <span id="S6.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> measures whether an agent commits the attacker-intended action on a single injected screenshot, not how an attack propagates through a multi-step interaction trajectory. We therefore do not measure whether later steps compound or correct an initial mis-action, or the downstream harm a successful injection causes.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">No benign success baseline.</span> We report attack success rate but not a paired benign task-success rate that would separate payload-induced failures from ordinary clean-task perception errors. The Generator’s ambiguity rule limits this confound by construction but does not remove it; a matched clean-versus-injected comparison is left to future work.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Sample diversity.</span> Because <span id="S6.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> expands a fixed pool of base screenshots into controlled per-intent variants rather than sampling independently authored screens, its outputs show lower CLIP screenshot dispersion and lower goal-text cluster entropy than hand-authored baselines (§<a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 RQ1: Generality and determinants ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>). The benchmark trades raw embedding diversity for balanced, controlled coverage; enlarging the base-screenshot pool would narrow this gap.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reliance on proprietary generative models.</span> The pipeline depends on closed VLM/LLM endpoints and an image-editing model (<span id="S6.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-image-2</span>) for localization, payload generation, and context-preserving rendering. This ties reproducibility and cost to third-party model availability, and although the Curator moderates render artefacts, some imperfect renders remain.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Realism measurement.</span> Absolute realism is hard to measure: human inter-annotator agreement is weak (Krippendorff <math id="S6.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.15</annotation></semantics></math>) and the LLM judge reads about one Likert point high. Our realism conclusions therefore rest on <em id="S6.p6.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">relative</em> comparisons that are robust to this noise (§<a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 RQ2: Stealth ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>) rather than on precise absolute scores.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Domain scope.</span> Our evaluation spans ten widely used, primarily English-language mobile applications and eleven attack intents. Generalisation to other languages, application categories, and to desktop or web GUI agents with different rendering and interaction conventions is untested.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Ethical Considerations</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Intended use.</span> <span id="S7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> is a benchmark-generation pipeline for security evaluation. It targets a weakness already present in VLM-based GUI agents: they cannot reliably separate trusted interface elements from attacker-controlled user-generated content. We intend it for red-teaming and robustness evaluation by developers and auditors before deployment, not for attacking live systems.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">No impact on live systems or users.</span> All experiments run offline on statically collected screenshots. We never posted injected content into any live application, targeted any production agent, or affected any real user or account; we use the applications only as visual substrates for controlled evaluation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dual-use and responsible release.</span> Because <span id="S7.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> produces working injection samples, it carries dual-use risk: the artefacts could in principle be repurposed against deployed agents, and our analysis of which regions are most exploitable could inform an adversary. We mitigate this by exposing a structural weakness of the screenshot-perception paradigm rather than introducing a new attack capability beyond current red-teaming practice, by using only publicly available applications and synthetic payloads, and by releasing the benchmark and code to support reproducible <em id="S7.p3.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">defense</em> research, which we judge to outweigh the marginal uplift to adversaries who already have these techniques.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Data and privacy.</span> The base screenshots were collected by the authors from public application interfaces and contain no personally identifiable information; incidental identifiers were removed, and all generated payloads are synthetic.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Human annotation.</span> The 200-sample realism study (§<a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 RQ2: Stealth ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>) was rated by three independent annotators on deidentified screenshots; we collected only realism judgements, with no personal data.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Large language model usage.</span> We used AI assistants to support drafting and code development. All AI-generated content was reviewed and verified by the authors for accuracy and originality.</p>
</div>
</section>
