</section>
<section id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Per-application and per-intent realism (auxiliary).</h4>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On the <span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span>-only LLM-judge subset, per-application means range from <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.65" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.65</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.65</annotation></semantics></math> (Telegram) to <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.69" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.69</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.69</annotation></semantics></math> (Facebook), and per-intent means range from <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.67" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.67</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.67</annotation></semantics></math> (<span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">enable_permission</span>) to <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.66" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.66</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.66</annotation></semantics></math> (<span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">follow_user</span>); the variation tracks rendering complexity and procedural-lure semantics rather than attack effectiveness (cf. the intent tiers of §<a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 RQ1: Generality and determinants ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>). Two limitations of these auxiliary numbers should be flagged: the LLM judge is over-lenient on short truncated payloads (e.g., <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">follow_user</span> samples with payload length <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 17</annotation></semantics></math> characters still receive realism <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.0</annotation></semantics></math>), which contributes to the <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px7.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim 1</annotation></semantics></math>-point inflation above; and no GhostEI realism comparison is included because its release contains no rendered screenshots that can be passed through either judge.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px8" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">RQ3 (Pipeline contribution):</h4>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">does each pipeline stage contribute independently to ASR, realism, or diversity?</em>
We compare the full pipeline against the three variants of Appendix <a href="#A2.SS3" title="B.3 Ablation Variants ‣ Appendix B Implementation Details ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a> on the ablation subset, using the two agents fixed after RQ1 (<span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px8.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-mini</span> and Qwen3-VL-32B, the most robust agent). We report ASR, realism, and diversity per variant. If a stage is necessary, removing it should produce a measurable drop in at least one metric: we expect <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Loc to reduce ASR, <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Gen to reduce realism or ASR, and <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Cur to reduce realism or diversity.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Caveats.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Four caveats apply to the ablation numbers. First, the variants have different sample sizes by design: Full (<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N{=}100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N{=}100</annotation></semantics></math>) is sub-sampled from the <span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> main set, while <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Loc (<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N{=}86" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>86</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N{=}86</annotation></semantics></math>), <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Gen (<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N{=}424" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>424</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N{=}424</annotation></semantics></math>), and <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Cur (<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N{=}195" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>195</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N{=}195</annotation></semantics></math>) are fresh Localizer<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>Generator reruns with the corresponding stage modified, so ASR and diversity differences partly reflect different (payload, intent) pools rather than pure variant isolation; realism differences are less affected because each sample is judged independently. Second, <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Loc covers only <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10/11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10/11</annotation></semantics></math> intents (missing <span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">inject_text</span>), so its aggregate ASR is computed over a smaller intent space and is not directly comparable to the other variants. Third, the Full row’s mean realism (<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.99</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.99</annotation></semantics></math>) is computed on the <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math>-sample ablation subset and is therefore lower than the <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.28</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.28</annotation></semantics></math> reported on the <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px9.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>200</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">200</annotation></semantics></math>-sample RQ2 subset (§<a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 RQ2: Stealth ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>); the two are not directly comparable. Fourth, Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct is the closest currently accessible substitute for a GUI-specialised agent; native GUI-specialized agents such as UI-TARS would require local GPU hosting and are not included in this submission.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.6 </span>Inference Configuration</h3>

<div id="A2.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All five agents are accessed through their respective inference APIs and wrapped in a unified action-prediction interface that maps a screenshot and a benign task instruction to a structured action. We use the OpenAI API for <span id="A2.SS6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-mini</span> and the SiliconFlow API for the remaining four models (<span id="A2.SS6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GLM-4.5V</span>, <span id="A2.SS6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct</span>, <span id="A2.SS6.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct</span>, <span id="A2.SS6.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct</span>). Within each model, the system prompt, decoding temperature, maximum new tokens, and output-format constraint are held fixed across all inputs; baselines and our method differ only in the input samples, not in the inference configuration. Exact model versions, API endpoints, decoding parameters, and prompt templates will be released with the camera-ready supplementary material.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.7 </span>Pipeline Decomposition: Ablation Results</h3>

<div id="A2.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section adds the per-criterion detail behind the RQ3 stage claims (§<a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 RQ3: Pipeline contribution ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>, Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.3 RQ2: Stealth ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>); the variant specifications are in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS3" title="B.3 Ablation Variants ‣ Appendix B Implementation Details ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>. The headline ASR, realism, diversity, and action-entropy figures are read off Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.3 RQ2: Stealth ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> in the main text. Two points are not visible there. First, the <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Gen realism drop (<math id="A2.SS7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.15</annotation></semantics></math>) falls on every rubric criterion and most sharply on <em id="A2.SS7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">semantic consistency</em> (<math id="A2.SS7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.64\to 3.50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.64</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>3.50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.64\to 3.50</annotation></semantics></math>) and <em id="A2.SS7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">detectability</em> (<math id="A2.SS7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.77\to 3.64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.77</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>3.64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.77\to 3.64</annotation></semantics></math>) of the UI-quality rubric (Appendix <a href="#A2.SS4" title="B.4 Realism Rubric ‣ Appendix B Implementation Details ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.4</span></a>), confirming that fixed-template payloads read as out-of-distribution system banners rather than authentic UI content. Second, the <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Loc heuristic almost never selects a text-input field, so it cannot generate <span id="A2.SS7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">inject_text</span> samples and covers only <math id="A2.SS7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10/11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10/11</annotation></semantics></math> intents, which is why its aggregate ASR is computed over a smaller intent space.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The three drop profiles are pairwise non-collinear—<math id="A2.SS7.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Loc reduces ASR and coverage with realism flat, <math id="A2.SS7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Gen reduces ASR and realism together, and <math id="A2.SS7.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Cur reduces realism and action balance with the smallest ASR effect—matching the per-stage predictions of Appendix <a href="#A2.SS3" title="B.3 Ablation Variants ‣ Appendix B Implementation Details ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a> and ruling out any Localizer<math id="A2.SS7.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>Generator or Generator<math id="A2.SS7.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>Curator collapse. Four ablation caveats (sample-size differences across variants, <math id="A2.SS7.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>Loc’s narrower intent coverage, the realism-subset mismatch, and the GUI-specialised-agent substitution) are in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS5" title="B.5 Per-RQ Procedure ‣ Appendix B Implementation Details ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.8 </span>Cross-Method Comparison: AgentHazard Paired Set</h3>

<div id="A2.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On the three-application overlap with AgentHazard (Spotify, Temu, X), we render AH’s <span id="A2.SS8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">adv_str</span> payloads onto AH’s screenshots via our PIL renderer and evaluate them on all five agents under the same per-intent ASR scoring (Table <a href="#A3.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ Appendix C Full Result Tables ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>). AH’s paired attacks achieve substantially higher ASR than <span id="A2.SS8.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> on every model, exceeding <span id="A2.SS8.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> by <math id="A2.SS8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>pp (Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B) to <math id="A2.SS8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>21</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">21</annotation></semantics></math>pp (<span id="A2.SS8.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-mini</span>). <span id="A2.SS8.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> is therefore not the most aggressive attack per sample on this overlap; §<a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 RQ2: Stealth ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> resolves this tension by showing that AH’s effectiveness advantage comes at a measurable plausibility cost, and that <span id="A2.SS8.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> occupies the high-plausibility end of an effectiveness–plausibility frontier. Two caveats apply. First, the overlap carries only two distinct attack intents (<span id="A2.SS8.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">status</span> and <span id="A2.SS8.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">click</span>; <span id="A2.SS8.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">navigate_home</span> is absent), so the paired set covers a narrower intent space than the full <span id="A2.SS8.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> main set. Second, AH’s broader threat model includes runtime accessibility overlays that can spawn modal windows and system UI; our paired comparison evaluates only the static-screenshot fragment of that threat model.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6: </span><span id="A3.T6.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">AgentHazard reaches <math id="A3.T6.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A3.T6.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>21</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">21</annotation></semantics></math>pp higher ASR than <span id="A3.T6.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> on the three-application overlap, but <span id="A3.T6.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> is far more realistic (<math id="A3.T6.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.19" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.19</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.19</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="A3.T6.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.64</annotation></semantics></math> LLM-judge, <math id="A3.T6.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.55" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.55</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.55</annotation></semantics></math>)—the effectiveness–plausibility tradeoff.</span> Paired comparison against AgentHazard <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> on the three-app overlap (Spotify, Temu, X); AH’s <span id="A3.T6.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">adv_str</span> and target bbox re-rendered via our PIL renderer under the shared intent-judge protocol. ASR: point estimates with <math id="A3.T6.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> Wilson CIs; realism: LLM-judge mean of four criteria. <span id="A3.T6.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bold</span> = higher value per row.</figcaption>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>CLIP t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) of 400 randomly sampled <span id="A3.F6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> screenshots, coloured by application. Each application forms multiple tight clusters (one per base screenshot’s variants), and the clusters spread across the embedding space rather than collapsing onto a few layouts.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 7: </span><span id="A3.T7.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Attack intent partitions into three tiers: temporal/attention lures (<span id="A3.T7.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">induce_wait</span> up to <math id="A3.T7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="88\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>88</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">88\%</annotation></semantics></math>) succeed far more than action-redirection or interaction-primitive intents (<span id="A3.T7.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">induce_back</span> <math id="A3.T7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 12\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 12\%</annotation></semantics></math>), stable across models.</span> Per-intent ASR (%) across the five agents, by descending average. <span id="A3.T7.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bold</span>/<span id="A3.T7.8" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">underline</span> = model’s most/second-most exploitable intent; gray = per-intent average.</figcaption>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 8: </span><span id="A3.T8.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE<span id="A3.T8.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright"> covers all four action categories where the baselines cover three, but trades embedding dispersion: its within-base variants give lower goal-text entropy and CLIP distance than independently authored baselines.</span></span> Cross-method diversity. <em id="A3.T8.12" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Goal-text entropy</em>: normalised <math id="A3.T8.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-means cluster entropy (<math id="A3.T8.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}8</annotation></semantics></math>) over goal embeddings; <em id="A3.T8.13" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">CLIP dist.</em>: mean cosine distance (CLIP ViT-B/32) on per-base dedup sub-samples (<sup id="A3.T8.14" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A3.T8.14.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup>one image per base, <span id="A3.T8.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span>’s 96 bases vs. AH’s 96 scenarios); <em id="A3.T8.16" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Action coverage</em>: the four §<a href="#A2.SS5" title="B.5 Per-RQ Procedure ‣ Appendix B Implementation Details ‣ MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a> categories with <math id="A3.T8.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> sample. <span id="A3.T8.17" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bold</span> = full coverage; gray = <span id="A3.T8.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">MIRAGE</span> rows.</figcaption>
